posts.name: HeroComplex
posts.cooked:
There have been at least two unlocks now.  Here's the link to the first screenshot, and my own is posted in response: https://twitter.com/esaka_jiro/status/667862847641161728

I went with the same line-up, environment, and villain as the first person did, for consistency.  Scholar, Nightmist, Haka, Ra, and Argent Adept vs. regular Gloomweaver in Realm of Discord.  The flavor for Scholar of the Infinite describes him as a gateway between reality and the void, which might indicate Realm of Discord is important.  From his screenshot and his comment that the unlock came after the end of match, Gloomweaver's turn must have just started and triggered a relic victory.  Second screenshot was also an end-of-game unlock, but otherwise did things a bit differently---brought Gloomweaver to 0 health during an incapped Scholar's turn, letting Haka use a power to fire a Savage Mana.  (Even with the other screenshot showing it wasn't necessary, it seemed like a very flavor-y way to do it.)  Since the Scholar of the Infinite text indicates says he "cannot protect himself," him being incapped is probably a necessary part of the unlock.  I also had two other heroes incapped, so even though there's flavor about Scholar protecting his allies, it seems like you don't need to keep everyone else alive.

So my current guess---beat Gloomweaver in Realm of Discord while Scholar is incapped.  Method of winning and whose turn it is don't seem to be important so far.  As for what cards are otherwise in play---looks like neither of us had any pins or Ophidian in play, so that could be relevant again, but it's hard to say from two examples whether any particular cards need to be absent or present.  Obviously, Scholar himself was incapped, so nothing of his was in play, for whatever that's worth.

posts.name: HeroComplex
posts.cooked:
I definitely get the flavor of Alchemical Redirection, but I don't think I ever played it.  I had 2 each of the Liquid and Energy elementals for a while---folks like Argent Adept letting me play Know When to Hold Fast on other player's turns made the discards pretty doable---and I think I had Flesh Into Iron in play for just one turn after it was pulled by Don't Dismiss Anything.  I let Flesh Into Iron expire because at that point I was ready to let him get Incapped, so I did have all three in play at one point (really, five total), but not right when he got flipped.  Pretty sure the incap came from a use of Haka's Taiaha---sent right at him, not redirected.  I also don't believe I ever used Expect the Worst or Get Out of the Way in that game, for whatever those are worth, but I'm pretty sure everything also saw play.  May have played Grace Under Fire once, not sure, and definitely played Know When to Turn Loose to self-damage for 12 when I was ready to get incapped.

 

Edit: By the way, in my unlock, Gloomweaver had just played Drum of Despair, which was the only relic of his I'd seen all game.  Since I was about to kill him with Savage Mana, I didn't bother with it.  So a Gloom relic in play should not prevent the unlock, and there were none in his discard for me---presumably all three for the other guy.

Got the unlock:

GW in Realm: we assume this is important

Vis, AA, Scholar, NM, and Haka (oddly fun team comp, slow to get going, but crazy fun synergy)

Played all forms, Alchemical Redirection, and several draw cards.

Scholar died to Haka's Taihia empowered by Haka of Battle with 1 liquid, 1 iron, and 3 energy out. Redirection was out at time of "death."

GW died to Vis auto damage card before Scholar used an incap power (plan was to use incap ability to win)

In summary I think it's:

GW in realm; Scholar incapped after using Redirection; fight on to victory.

Forms might be needed, but I think that might be just making things more complicated than it has to be.
